issues.title: New regression test is flaky: rpc::stream_closed escapes the test body at smp>1
issues.verdictReason: Built build/dev and ran the new case 60x with `-- -c2`: 4 runs failed with `fatal error: in "test_stream_send_after_stream_close": seastar::rpc::stream_closed: rpc stream was closed by peer` (0/40 at -c1). The client's stream_close()->stop() tears the connection down, the server's stream read loop hits EOF, sets _error and runs _stream_queue.abort(stream_closed()) (src/rpc/rpc.cc:1285) before the server fiber's `while (source().get()) {}` consumed the queued eof marker; the throw escapes seastar::async and surfaces at server_done.get().
issues.scopeReason: The PR adds this test; test.py's default --smp 2 makes it fail roughly 7% of runs.

reportedAs.rafp-detailed: New regression test is flaky (~8% failure rate). The server fiber does sink.close() then drains source(); when stream_close() causes the reader to hit EOF, _stream_queue.abort() discards the queued eof marker and source() throws rpc::stream_closed, which escapes the test body uncaught (existing tests wrap this in check_exception). Measured 7/60 standalone failures and 2/12 whole-suite failures at --mode=dev -c2.
reportedAs.ce-code-review: Test's server-handler read loop may raise stream_closed during normal shutdown and escape server_done.get() (retained as residual risk only, with no demonstrated trigger).

issues.title: stream_close() now gates write_buf.close()/stop()/abort() behind an unbounded queue drain
issues.verdictReason: src/rpc/rpc.cc:565-572 chains write_buf.close() and then stop() after `queue_drained`. Pre-PR write_buf.close() ran immediately and its `_fd.close()` is posix_data_sink_impl::close() = `_fd.shutdown(SHUT_WR)` (src/net/posix-stack.cc:894-897), which is exactly what unwedges a send_entry() parked in pollable_fd::write_all() on a full peer window; stop()->abort()->shutdown_input() (rpc.cc:353-359) is likewise what ends the receive loop so stop_send_loop() can call shutdown_output() (rpc.cc:200-202). Both escape hatches are now downstream of the very write they would have to break, so a frame parked on peer backpressure leaves the connection, its fd and its buffers hung with no timeout.
issues.scopeReason: The drain wait is added by this PR's own hunk.

reportedAs.builtin-code-review: stream_close() now defers stop()/abort()/shutdown_input() behind outgoing-queue drain, allowing hangs. Previously write_buf.close() returned promptly even with a write in flight and the immediate stop() eventually caused stop_send_loop() to call shutdown_output() and break a stalled send.
reportedAs.ce-code-review: stream_close() gates stop()/abort() behind an unbounded queue drain. abort() is the only mechanism that can fail a stuck low-level write; if a frame is parked on peer backpressure, queue_drained never resolves and the connection's fd, buffers, and teardown state leak forever with no timeout or cancellation.
reportedAs.mattpocock-review: New outgoing-queue drain can gate/hang the abort path via sink.close(). A front entry stuck in send_entry() behind TCP backpressure from a live-but-not-reading peer can hang sink.close() with shutdown_output() sequestered behind it.
reportedAs.superpowers-review: The drain wait is unbounded; the comment would be more useful naming what breaks it (stop_send_loop's shutdown_output) rather than only who no longer waits. Not a regression.
reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: (self-rejected) Reviewer checked for a new deadlock from deferring write_buf.close() and found none: pre-PR the same socket flush already gated stop().
reportedAs.rafp-review: (withdrawn) Candidate risk that stream_close() could hang waiting on the drained _outgoing_queue_ready before stop() runs.

issues.title: Unguarded put(std::span) override breaks the build at SEASTAR_API_LEVEL 7 and 8
issues.verdictReason: Compiled tests/unit/rpc_test.cc with -fsyntax-only at -DSEASTAR_API_LEVEL=8 and =7: three hard errors ('marked override, but does not override', 'no matching function for call to seastar::data_sink::put(std::span<...>&)', 'invalid new-expression of abstract class type'). The same file from main compiles clean at level 8. data_sink_impl::put(std::span) is behind `#if SEASTAR_API_LEVEL >= 9` (include/seastar/core/iostream.hh:110-128); loopback_socket.hh:144-153 already uses the required #if/#else pattern, and configure.py --api-level still accepts 7/8.
issues.scopeReason: The offending override is added by this PR and main builds fine at those levels.

reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: Unguarded put(span) override breaks build below API level 9; the build breaks with three errors since the test doesn't use the existing #if SEASTAR_API_LEVEL >= 9 fallback pattern used elsewhere.
reportedAs.builtin-code-review: test_data_sink_impl fails to compile at SEASTAR_API_LEVEL 7/8; the class is abstract and the override refers to nothing, causing a hard compile error.
reportedAs.ce-code-review: test_data_sink_impl's put(std::span) override isn't guarded by SEASTAR_API_LEVEL, breaking the build at levels CMakeLists.txt still offers.
reportedAs.rafp-detailed: test_data_sink_impl override breaks build at SEASTAR_API_LEVEL < 9; compiling with --api-level 8 fails with 'marked override, but does not override'; loopback_socket.hh already guards the equivalent method.
reportedAs.tob-diff-review: The override is unguarded but that member only exists under SEASTAR_API_LEVEL >= 9; below 9 this causes an override-of-nothing error and leaves the class abstract.
reportedAs.scoped-detailed: Test build is not portable across environments.

issues.title: Regression test never asserts the send was refused; closed_error is swallowed
issues.verdictReason: tests/unit/rpc_test.cc:2016-2021 is `try { stream_send_empty_frame().get(); } catch (const rpc::closed_error&) { }` with no assertion in either branch. The PR's whole added contract (send() fails once stream_close() has begun) is therefore unasserted; the only check left is the indirect BOOST_REQUIRE_MESSAGE(!st.put_after_close) at :2030. BOOST_REQUIRE_THROW would pin it.
issues.scopeReason: The test is added by this PR.

reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: try/catch around stream_send_empty_frame().get() asserts nothing in either branch, so if send() wrongly accepts the frame the test still passes; only a second-order check that depends on poller timing catches it.
reportedAs.ce-code-review: The refused send()'s closed_error is caught by a bare try/catch and discarded with nothing asserted, so the test's only real signal is an indirect timing-dependent check.
reportedAs.mattpocock-review: stream_send_empty_frame().get() is wrapped in a try with an empty catch(closed_error&), so nothing requires the throw; BOOST_REQUIRE_THROW would pin it properly.
reportedAs.rafp-review: The new test calls the captured send_empty_frame hook inside a try/catch that silently swallows rpc::closed_error, so the PR's added contract is never actually asserted.
reportedAs.superpowers-review: The test never asserts the send was refused; catch (closed_error&) {} swallows the success case too.
reportedAs.tob-diff-review: The try/catch (const rpc::closed_error&) passes whether or not the frame is rejected; needs BOOST_REQUIRE_THROW or a BOOST_FAIL after the .get().
reportedAs.scoped-detailed: Reproducer test is missing an assertion.

issues.title: Queue-drain half of the fix has no test coverage at all
issues.verdictReason: Verified by experiment: reverting only the std::exchange/then_wrapped hunk (keeping _stream_closing) and rebuilding leaves the new test passing 20/20. The cause is structural: sink_impl::close() awaits the eof-marker send() before `f.finally([con]{ return con->close_sink(); })` (include/seastar/rpc/rpc_impl.hh:911-924), so _outgoing_queue is already empty and queue_drained is already resolved when stream_close() runs. The exceptional branch (then_wrapped/ignore_ready_future) and the concurrent stop_send_loop() interleaving are likewise never exercised.
issues.scopeReason: This is the riskier half of the PR's own fix (see I2) and the PR is where its test belongs.

reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: Deleting lines 562-568 (the queue_drained handling) leaves the new regression test passing, so this riskier half of the fix, which changes what stop_send_loop() sees, is untested.
reportedAs.ce-code-review: The then_wrapped/ignore_ready_future() branch is never exercised because the new test only ever queues an eof marker that always succeeds; also no test drives _outgoing_queue_ready to be non-ready at the moment stream_close() runs, and no test covers stop_send_loop() running concurrently with a parked stream_close().
reportedAs.rafp-detailed: The new test only exercises the case where close() is parked with an empty queue, so the drain logic is a no-op in that test; reverting just the drain leaves the whole suite green.
reportedAs.tob-diff-review: _outgoing_queue is empty when the test reaches stream_close() because sink_impl::close() awaits the eof-marker send() before calling close_sink(); reverting the std::exchange/then_wrapped hunk while keeping _stream_closing still leaves the new test green.

issues.title: Server compressor factory's hooks vector is mutated cross-shard by negotiate()
issues.verdictReason: server_factory is a stack local on shard 0, but loopback_socket_impl::connect() round-robins server connections via _factory.next_shard() (tests/unit/loopback_socket.hh:343-345), so at --smp 2 the stream connection's server side negotiates on shard 1 and runs const_cast<...>(this)->hooks.push_back(...) against a shard-0 std::vector, concurrently with shard 0's own push_back for the parent connection. That is an unsynchronised cross-shard mutation plus a shard-1 allocation later freed on shard 0.
issues.scopeReason: The factory and its cross-shard use are added by this PR.

reportedAs.superpowers-review: server_factory lives on shard 0 but loopback_socket_impl::connect round-robins server connections, so at default --smp 2 the stream connection's negotiate() runs const_cast<...>(this)->hooks.push_back(...) on shard 1 against a shard-0 vector — unsynchronized mutation with a buffer allocated by shard 1's allocator and freed by shard 0, which is UB that ASan/UBSan won't catch.
reportedAs.rafp-detailed: The factory is shared across shards, and negotiate() const_casts and push_backs into it from both shard 0 and shard 1; no failure is observable today because server hooks are unused.

issues.title: Comment claims nothing else waits on _outgoing_queue_ready, but stop_send_loop() does
issues.verdictReason: src/rpc/rpc.cc:559-561 says 'Nothing else waits for _outgoing_queue_ready from here on: ... stop_send_loop() waits for _sink_closed_future.' stop_send_loop() literally does `when_all(std::move(_outgoing_queue_ready), std::move(_sink_closed_future))` at rpc.cc:225. The load-bearing property is that after the exchange that wait is vacuous and the drain guarantee flows through _sink_closed_future instead; the comment does not say that, which is what protects the pair from being reordered.
issues.scopeReason: The comment is new in this PR.

reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: The comment says nothing else waits for _outgoing_queue_ready, but stop_send_loop() does wait on it; the real point (that the wait becomes vacuous after the exchange, with the drain guarantee flowing through _sink_closed_future) is nowhere stated.
reportedAs.mattpocock-review: The comment claims stop_send_loop() waits only on _sink_closed_future, but it still waits on both futures; the real safety property is that the queue-ready wait is subsumed by _sink_closed_future.
reportedAs.tob-diff-review: The comment states 'Nothing else waits for _outgoing_queue_ready from here on', but stop_send_loop() does wait on it, at src/rpc/rpc.cc:225; the code itself is correct, but the comment misstates it.

issues.title: Comment names the wrong cause for an exceptional _outgoing_queue_ready
issues.verdictReason: src/rpc/rpc.cc:566 says '_outgoing_queue_ready is exceptional if an entry failed'. send()'s own continuation swallows send_entry() failures (`if (f.failed()) { f.ignore_ready_future(); abort(); } p->done.set_value();`, rpc.cc:333-338), so a failed entry resolves the chain normally. The real sources are withdraw(it, ex) (rpc.cc:288) and stop_send_loop()'s `it->done.set_exception(ex)` / `_negotiated->set_exception(ex)` — which the neighbouring pre-existing comment at rpc.cc:226-227 states correctly.
issues.scopeReason: The comment is new in this PR.

reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: The new comment claims _outgoing_queue_ready is exceptional if an entry failed, but entry failures are swallowed by send()'s continuation; the real causes are withdraw(it, ex) and _negotiated->set_exception() from a concurrent stop_send_loop().
reportedAs.rafp-review: (left out of scope) The comment stating '_outgoing_queue_ready is exceptional if an entry failed' is inaccurate: a failed send_entry() calls abort() and then still calls p->done.set_value(), so entry failure resolves the chain normally.

issues.title: Lambda parameter f shadows the function-scope f it is being assigned to
issues.verdictReason: `auto f = make_ready_future<>();` at rpc.cc:549 and the continuation parameter `(future<> f)` at rpc.cc:565 inside the statement assigning that same f; the one place an exception is deliberately discarded reads as f = ...f....
issues.scopeReason: Introduced by this PR's hunk.

reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: The lambda parameter f shadows the function-scope f being assigned, making the statement read as f = ...f... in the one place an exception is deliberately discarded; should be renamed to drained.
reportedAs.mattpocock-review: The lambda parameter named f shadows the outer f declared at rpc.cc:549, inside the assignment to that same variable; should be renamed to drained.
reportedAs.superpowers-review: The inner lambda param f shadows the auto f from line 549, in the statement assigning the outer one.

issues.title: Docs overstate that both halves of a stream must always be closed
issues.verdictReason: connection::_sink_closed and _source_closed both default to true (include/seastar/rpc/rpc.hh:300-301) and are only cleared by sink_impl's and source_impl's constructors (rpc_impl.hh:839, :494). A connection on which the application was only ever handed a sink therefore reaches stream_check_twoway_closed() with no source involved, so 'both halves' should read 'each half you were given'. Same wording on rpc::sink's new doxygen block (rpc_types.hh:341-342).
issues.scopeReason: The sentence is added by this PR.

reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: The doc and rpc_types.hh both claim shutdown requires both halves closed, but _sink_closed and _source_closed default to true and are only cleared by the respective impl constructors, so a connection with only a sink never needs a source to close for stream_close() to run.
reportedAs.superpowers-review: "Both halves of a stream must be closed" overstates it; with no returned sink, _source_closed is true from construction (rpc.hh:301), so the doc should say "each half you were given".

issues.title: "Shut down only once both halves are closed" ignores error and peer-driven teardown
issues.verdictReason: doc/rpc-streaming.md:115 says the connection is shut down 'only once both halves are closed', which contradicts the same file's line 49 ('closing the client aborts any stream still open on it') and the error paths in src/rpc/rpc.cc:1062-1067 and :1284-1289 that tear the stream down regardless. The word 'only' should go.
issues.scopeReason: The sentence is added by this PR.

reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: Line 115's claim that the stream shuts down only once both halves are closed contradicts line 49's statement that closing the client aborts any stream still open on it; error paths and peer shutdown also tear it down, so "only" should be dropped.

issues.title: #closing-a-stream anchor does not resolve in the doxygen build
issues.verdictReason: doc/rpc-streaming.md is in doxygen's INPUT (doc/Doxyfile.in:764) and MARKDOWN_ID_STYLE is absent from Doxyfile.in, so doxygen 1.9.8 (the version installed here) uses its default DOXYGEN id style and gives headings autotoc_md<N> ids rather than GitHub slugs. The link is the only markdown anchor reference in any of the four doxygen-fed .md files, so there is no working precedent to copy.
issues.scopeReason: The link is added by this PR.

reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: Because MARKDOWN_ID_STYLE is unset in Doxyfile.in, header IDs become autotoc_md<N> rather than GitHub slugs, so the #closing-a-stream anchor resolves on GitHub but produces an unresolved-reference warning and renders as plain text in the generated API docs.

issues.title: send_empty_frame's contract comment not updated for the widened closed_error window

This PR makes it fail with closed_error for the whole of stream_close(), a window in which it previously succeeded, and the hook is the one API whose failure mode the change widens. Nothing tells callers the failure is expected rather than fatal.
issues.scopeReason: The PR widens this API's failure window and commit 3 documents sink/source but not this.

reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: The PR makes send_empty_frame newly fail with closed_error in a window where it previously succeeded, but the doc comment still only describes the old behavior and doesn't warn callers not to treat the failure as fatal.
reportedAs.superpowers-review: Commit 3 documents sink and source but not send_empty_frame, the one API whose failure mode this PR widens.
reportedAs.rafp-review: (withdrawn) Candidate finding that the send_empty_frame contract comment lacks a note that it may fail.

issues.title: Parked data_sink::close() is released on the happy path only, with no scope guard
issues.verdictReason: tests/unit/rpc_test.cc:2026 `st.release_close.set_value();` is a bare straight-line statement after the try/catch at :2016-2021 and the yield loop at :2022-2024. Any exception other than rpc::closed_error escaping that region leaves the connection parked in output_stream::close() and stop_send_loop(), so the test hangs to the 300s harness timeout or trips ~sink_impl's SEASTAR_ASSERT instead of failing cleanly — even though seastar/util/defer.hh is already included by the file.
issues.scopeReason: The parked-close mechanism is added by this PR.

reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: st.release_close.set_value() is a bare statement; any throw between lines 2011 and 2025 leaves it unsatisfied, causing ~sink_impl's SEASTAR_ASSERT to fire or the test to hang instead of producing a diagnosable failure, even though defer is already included.
reportedAs.ce-code-review: st.release_close.set_value() sits on the straight-line happy path after the try/catch, so any exception other than closed_error escaping the guarded region leaves the connection blocked in output_stream::close() and stop_send_loop(), wedging the test until the 300s harness timeout.

issues.title: close_entered_cv.wait() has no timeout, so a regression hangs rather than fails
issues.verdictReason: tests/unit/rpc_test.cc:2011 is `st.close_entered_cv.wait([&] { return st.close_entered; }).get()` with no deadline; condition_variable::wait has timeout overloads. If a future change stops stream_close() from reaching the wrapped data_sink::close(), the test hangs to the harness timeout instead of reporting a failure.
issues.scopeReason: The wait is added by this PR.

reportedAs.ce-code-review: st.close_entered_cv.wait(...) at :2011 has no timeout, so a regression preventing stream_close() from being entered hangs the test rather than failing it cleanly.

issues.title: Test cannot distinguish a refusal caused by _stream_closing from one caused by _error
issues.verdictReason: connection::send() returns make_exception_future<>(closed_error()) for both `_error` and `_stream_closing` (src/rpc/rpc.cc:293, :341). The comment at rpc_test.cc:2013-2015 asserts '_error is not yet set' but nothing checks it, so a future change that made the test pass because _error got set early would go unnoticed.
issues.scopeReason: The test and the claim it makes are added by this PR.

reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: send() returns closed_error for both _stream_closing and _error, and the test comment claims _error is not yet set but nothing checks it; the ordering that makes the test pass for the right reason is a race the fix could lose without failing the test.

issues.title: server_factory is wired up but never read; the server side of the fix is untested
issues.verdictReason: server_factory.hooks is populated by negotiate() but never read anywhere in the test; only client_factory.hooks is consulted (rpc_test.cc:2000-2001). The fix sits in connection::stream_close(), shared by server::connection, whose teardown additionally runs abort_all_streams()/deregister_this_stream() (src/rpc/rpc.cc:1290-1294), so 'same base function' is not full coverage.
issues.scopeReason: The test is added by this PR and already builds the server-side scaffolding.

reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: server_factory is wired up and never read; the symmetric server-side case is untested, and server teardown (including abort_all_streams()) differs enough from the client's that "same base function" isn't a complete argument for coverage.
reportedAs.mattpocock-review: Spec says the same code serves server::connection so the server side is exposed too, but the test only drives the client; server_factory's hooks are never read, existing only to make negotiation succeed.

issues.title: server_done initialised to make_ready_future<>() makes its check vacuous
issues.verdictReason: tests/unit/rpc_test.cc:1978 declares `future<> server_done = make_ready_future<>();` and only the handler body overwrites it, so server_done.get() at :2028 succeeds silently if the handler never ran. A std::optional<future<>> or an explicit 'handler ran' flag would catch that.
issues.scopeReason: The test is added by this PR.

reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: future<> server_done = make_ready_future<>() means server_done.get() at line 2028 passes silently even if the server handler never ran.

issues.title: test_sink_state is declared inside the lambda body but outlived by the rpc connection
issues.verdictReason: `test_sink_state st;` is declared inside the do_with_thread body at rpc_test.cc:1977, while the wrappers holding `test_sink_state&` (test_socket_impl, test_connected_socket_impl, test_data_sink_impl) are owned by the rpc stream connection, which deferred_stop(cl) in rpc_test_env::do_with_thread (rpc_test.cc:268) tears down only after the body returns. Nothing touches _st on that path today, so this is latent, but server_factory/client_factory are already declared outside for exactly this reason and st should follow.
issues.scopeReason: The declaration is added by this PR.

reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: test_sink_state st is declared inside the lambda body, but wrappers holding test_sink_state& are owned by the rpc connection, which deferred_stop(cl) tears down after the body returns; latent since nothing touches _st on that path today.
reportedAs.ce-code-review: st is captured by reference by objects whose lifetime follows RPC-internal shared_ptr refcounting rather than C++ scope; declaring st first is protective only if dropping sink and source synchronously releases the last reference.

issues.title: Hardcoded hooks.size()==2u plus hooks.back() pins the fixture's connection count and order
issues.verdictReason: rpc_test.cc:2000-2001 asserts client_factory.hooks.size()==2u and then binds `auto&` to hooks.back(). Both client connections are created on shard 0 in a fixed order, so this is deterministic today and the reference cannot be invalidated between :2001 and its use at :2017 (no further client negotiation happens in between) — but a change to rpc_test_env setup would silently retarget the test, and recording the size before make_stream_sink and copying the std::function costs nothing.
issues.scopeReason: Both lines are added by this PR.

reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: BOOST_REQUIRE_EQUAL(hooks.size(), 2u) hardcodes the fixture's connection count rather than testing the code under test, and the reference from hooks.back() could dangle if a push_back happens before it's used 16 lines later.
reportedAs.superpowers-review: hooks.size() == 2 plus hooks.back() hardcodes loopback's shard/ordering policy, and capturing auto& into a growing std::vector is invalidated by any later negotiation.
reportedAs.tob-diff-review: BOOST_REQUIRE_EQUAL(hooks.size(), 2u) plus hooks.back() hard-codes both the count and order of client-side negotiations, so a change to rpc_test_env setup would silently retarget the test.

issues.title: buffer_size() hardcodes 8192 instead of forwarding to _inner
issues.verdictReason: Every other member of test_data_sink_impl forwards to _inner; buffer_size() returns a literal 8192. The claimed behavioural divergence does not exist though: connection::socket_and_buffers builds write_buf with `fd.output()` (include/seastar/rpc/rpc.hh:247) and connected_socket::output takes `size_t buffer_size = 8192` (include/seastar/net/api.hh:226), so data_sink_impl::buffer_size() is never consulted on this path. It is dead code that should say so or forward.
issues.scopeReason: The method is added by this PR.

reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: buffer_size() is hardcoded to 8192; verified dead since connected_socket::output() passes an explicit default of 8192 so the sink's value is never consulted, but this should be stated in a comment.
reportedAs.mattpocock-review: Every sibling method forwards to _inner, but buffer_size() returns a hardcoded 8192 and should call _inner.buffer_size().
reportedAs.tob-diff-review: connected_socket::output() passes buffer_size = 0, so the stream under test adopts 8192 instead of the real sink's size, an unnecessary divergence from production in a reproducer.

issues.title: const_cast used to record hooks instead of a mutable member or a tracker reference
issues.verdictReason: rpc_test.cc:1957 is `const_cast<hook_capturing_compressor_factory*>(this)->hooks.push_back(...)` inside a const virtual; declaring `mutable std::vector<...> hooks` removes it, and the adjacent factory near rpc_test.cc:1801 already does the same job via a tracker& member.
issues.scopeReason: The const_cast is added by this PR.

reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: const_cast<...*>(this)->hooks.push_back(...) is used instead of declaring hooks mutable.
reportedAs.mattpocock-review: const_cast<hook_capturing_compressor_factory*>(this)->hooks.push_back(...) dodges constness, while the adjacent factory (~line 1801) does the same job cleanly via a tracker& member.
reportedAs.tob-diff-review: A const_cast is used only because the factories are non-const locals; making hooks mutable would avoid the const_cast.

issues.title: negotiate(feature, is_server) calls abort(), killing the binary with no Boost.Test diagnostic
issues.verdictReason: rpc_test.cc:1960 `std::unique_ptr<rpc::compressor> negotiate(sstring, bool) const override { abort(); }` terminates the whole test binary via SIGABRT with no test name or location. issues.title: _outgoing_queue_ready is left ready while the tail-entry invariant can still be re-established
issues.verdictReason: After the exchange at rpc.cc:562, _outgoing_queue_ready is a ready future while entries may still be linked in _outgoing_queue, breaking its documented role as the tail entry's done future. Nothing enqueues after that point today — send() is refused by the new _stream_closing check and client::enqueue_zero_frame() (rpc.cc:866-884) only runs from the client constructor — but enqueue_zero_frame() guards on `_error` alone, so its exchange is not covered by the new flag, and any future enqueue path that misses the check would fire its continuation immediately and reopen the race this PR closes.
issues.scopeReason: The exchange that breaks the invariant is added by this PR.

issues.title: Safety of the stream_close()/stop_send_loop() interleaving rests on an unrecorded ordering assumption
issues.verdictReason: stop_send_loop() sets `_error = true` at rpc.cc:199 and reaches the `when_all(std::move(_outgoing_queue_ready), ...)` at :225 with no suspension point in between, which is the only reason stream_close()'s `if (!error())` guard at :550 reliably keeps the new std::exchange at :562 off a moved-from future. Nothing in either function records that dependency, so inserting a co_await or early return between :199 and :225 would silently break it.
issues.scopeReason: The PR adds the second move of _outgoing_queue_ready that makes the ordering load-bearing.

reportedAs.ce-code-review: The interleaving is safe only because stop_send_loop() sets _error = true synchronously with no suspension point before the when_all at :225; a future co_await or early return between those points would let stream_close()'s if (!error()) guard fail to protect the new std::exchange from a moved-from future, and nothing in the code records this dependency.

issues.title: sink::close() can now fail where it previously succeeded, undocumented

Deferring the call past the new suspension point at rpc.cc:565 widens the window in which the peer can tear the connection down and leave an _ex behind. The failure mode pre-dates the PR, but the widening is not mentioned in the commit message or PR body.
issues.scopeReason: The PR widens the window; a sentence in the commit message would cover it.

reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: Deferring write_buf.close() past a suspension point widens the failure window: if the peer tears down the connection while the drain is parked, output_stream::close() can rethrow a stored exception, a change not mentioned in the commit message or PR body.

issues.title: Re-entry into stream_close() is still guarded only by error(), not by the new _stream_closing flag
issues.verdictReason: rpc.cc:550 guards only on `!error()`, which stays false for the whole of the new drain-and-close await, so a second close_sink()/close_source() reaching stream_close() in that window would overwrite _sink_closed_future and close write_buf twice. Reachability is low (it needs source::make_sink() to reopen the sink half after both halves closed), and the window existed before the PR because write_buf.close() was already asynchronous — but the PR lengthens it, and `&& !_stream_closing` is now free.
issues.scopeReason: The PR lengthens the unguarded window and introduces the flag that would close it.

reportedAs.superpowers-review: Re-entry into stream_close() is guarded only by error(), which is false for the whole new await; reachability is low (needs source::make_sink() re-open) and the issue is pre-existing, but adding !error() && !_stream_closing is free.
